children: Tesla (TSLA) got a BBB investment‑grade rating from Fitch. Stock traded near $376.25. Fitch said low default risk; rating may affect Tesla’s financing for AI and manufacturing.
NHTSA opened two public probes into Tesla (TSLA): one on camera-only FSD crashes in glare, fog and dust; another on FSD vehicles running red lights or wrong-way, some causing injuries.
Tesla (TSLA) plans over $25B capex in 2026 for AI chips, data centers, production lines and AI vehicles. Planned spend equals about 57% of Q2 cash, investments and equivalents.
Tesla (TSLA) had about 1.48M paid FSD subscribers as of June 30, up 16% QoQ. FSD-powered robotaxis are operating in parts of Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa.
Traders watch Tesla (TSLA) revenue split, fleet buyer count and committed vehicles for Cybercab—key metrics for recurring revenue vs one‑time sales and for fleet scale.
Tesla’s Cybercab model: if external fleets fund vehicles while Tesla keeps software, booking, pricing and dispatch, Tesla would record vehicle sales and earn recurring per-ride platform fees.
Goldman cut Tesla (TSLA) Q3 deliveries to 435,000 from 490,000 and lowered Q4, citing weaker sales in China, the US and Europe and a slimmer product lineup after two model discontinuations.
Regulatory and competitive risks cloud Tesla’s robotaxi and autonomy plans; analysts also questioned whether slowing vehicle deliveries could hurt TSLA’s car business growth.
TSLA valuation hinges on self-driving software, Optimus robot program and AI initiatives rather than just quarterly vehicle deliveries—key drivers for traders to watch.
Analyst predicts ~80% chance Tesla (TSLA) will merge with SpaceX by end of 2027; says combined firm could be largest globally due to integrated AI initiatives.
